subject: Cooking
title: Fusion Cuisine: When Cultures Collide on a Plate
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Fusion Cuisine: When Cultures Collide on a Plate.

hook.text: Korean tacos, sushi burritos, and tikka masala pizza — fusion cuisine breaks every rule of tradition.

buildup.text: Fusion started in 1980s Los Angeles where immigrant communities lived side by side and kitchens overlapped.

discovery.text: Chef Roy Choi's Kogi BBQ truck — Korean short ribs in Mexican tortillas — launched the modern fusion movement.

twist.text: Critics call fusion 'confusion.' But every cuisine is already fused — Italian food without tomatoes was pre-1500.

climax.text: Peru's Nikkei cuisine (Japanese-Peruvian) is now Michelin-celebrated — proof that fusion creates new classics.

punchline.text: Every great cuisine was once a fusion. We just forgot the mixing.

details.summary: When cultures collide through immigration, colonization, or trade, their cuisines inevitably merge. Tex-Mex, Japanese-Peruvian Nikkei, and Indian-British curry house food all emerged from cultural collision rather than deliberate chef experimentation.
details.whyItMatters: Collision fusion happens whether intentional or not, and produces some of the world's most beloved cuisines. Recognizing that cultural contact always generates new food traditions challenges the concept of culinary purity.
takeaways: Tex-Mex, Nikkei, and Anglo-Indian cuisines all emerged from cultural collision
Immigration is the most powerful force creating new food traditions
No cuisine is pure — all are products of historical mixing and adaptation

faq.question: How does immigration create new cuisines?
faq.answer: Immigrants adapt their home cooking with locally available ingredients. Chinese immigrants in Peru created chifa using local peppers and Chinese techniques. Indian immigrants in Britain created dishes like chicken tikka masala that exist in neither traditional Indian nor British cooking.

faq.question: What makes collision fusion different from restaurant fusion?
faq.answer: Collision fusion emerges organically from daily life — immigrant families cooking with what is available. Restaurant fusion is a deliberate creative act by chefs combining traditions. Collision fusion is lived experience; restaurant fusion is artistic choice.
